correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and 0<q<1, positive geometrically decreasing increments form a convex cone on which Aitken is smooth. Its row differential equals (t^2,-2t,1)/(1-t)^2. Decomposing every perturbation into adjacent steps and checking each truncated four-level response gives the stated exact n=3,4,5,>=6 constants. Segment integration proves the two-input inequality; geometric-ratio interior signals and infinitesimal admissible steps approach each coefficient. A separately executed ordinary rational checker verified 624 algebraic identities, 27,000 derivative bounds, 2,700 two-input tests and 24 limiting witnesses. These finite checks corroborate, but do not replace, the analytical proof.

value.rationale: Aitken eliminates exactly geometric errors, but this does not bound roughness of the difference of two perturbed transformed sequences. The exact variation modulus on a natural q-linear convergence cone exhibits a genuine four-input step-location transition at q=1/2, a five-input intermediate regime, length saturation at six, and sharp quadratic blow-up at q approaching one. This is a complete, mathematically motivated sharp nonlinear stability classification, not a routine algebraic equivalence or an arbitrary numerical sample.
